tasks.prompt: Windows resolves program names case-insensitively, but three of the guard's rules in internal/tools/guard.go match the program name in one case only: disk (`Format D:` or `FORMAT D:` passes), pipe-to-shell (`curl ... | PowerShell -` passes, and `| iex` / `Invoke-Expression` is not matched as a shell at all), and sudo (Windows 11 ships sudo, and `Sudo` passes). Make the program-name part of these three rules case-insensitive on every platform, and make pipe-to-shell also match irm and iwr as downloaders and iex and Invoke-Expression as the shell, with tests in internal/tools/guard_test.go. Tools whose subcommands are case-sensitive (gh, kubectl, docker, helm, terraform) need no change. Do not run git on this repository.

Investigate this report: hrn gc --idle 0 should remove every build cache, yet TestGCTakesTheIdleLimitAsGiven in internal/gc/cache_test.go failed once on Windows with "fresh: got keep (last written 0m ago, inside --idle 0m), want remove". A cache written moments before compared as not older than now (file timestamps and the wall clock differ by their resolution, so the age can be zero or slightly negative), and the "inside --idle" rule then kept it. Fix it in internal/gc/cache.go so that --idle 0 means any age, including a clock difference: add a helper ageAt(now, written time.Time) time.Duration that returns how long before now a cache was written and 0 when the write time is at or after now, and use it wherever gc compares a cache's age with an idle limit (the --idle decision and --free-below's minimum idle time). Add a test for a write time a moment after now, and make the existing test write its fresh cache a second in the past. Do not run git on this repository.

hrn watch --public exempts page navigations (GET or HEAD with Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate) from the Origin check in the guard handler of internal/watch/server.go. That exemption also covers iframe, object and embed loads, which carry the same mode. Require Sec-Fetch-Dest: document as well, so that only top-level page loads are exempt: a cross-site GET with Sec-Fetch-Dest: iframe, or with no Sec-Fetch-Dest at all, is refused with 403 and logged with the reason "bad origin", while a cross-site GET or HEAD with Sec-Fetch-Dest: document and a valid token still passes. Add the cases to internal/watch/access_test.go. Do not run git on this repository.

In internal/remote/client.go, Watch treats only ErrMalformedEvent and ErrEventOutput as terminal and resets its failure count on every 200 response, so an SSE line over 1 MiB (the scanner in ReadEvents fails with bufio.ErrTooLong) is fetched again from the same cursor once a second, for ever. Make ReadEvents report such a line as an error whose text says "event line exceeds 1 MiB limit" and that wraps bufio.ErrTooLong, and make Watch return that error instead of retrying, so a server that sends an oversized line is asked exactly once. Add a test in internal/remote/client_test.go that Watch returns the error after one request. Do not run git on this repository.

hrn watch shortens a quoted program path in a system folder to its file name ("C:\Program Files\Git (Preview)\bin\bash.exe" becomes "bash.exe"), but a double-quoted path whose folder contains an apostrophe ("C:\Program Files\Bob's Tools\tool.exe" --help) is still shown in full, because the scan in the function program in internal/watch/paths.go stops at either quote character. Make only the matching quote end a quoted path, for double and single quotes alike and for their JSON-escaped spellings, so that path shortens to "tool.exe" --help in plain text and in JSON text. An unterminated quote still stops at the input's end or a line end. Inside a single-quoted path in JSON text, an unescaped double quote still ends the scan, since it closes the JSON string, so an unterminated single quote stops at the string's end and the next field is kept; an even run of backslashes before that double quote escapes only itself. Add the cases to internal/watch/paths_test.go. Do not run git on this repository.

parseCodexStream in internal/agent/codex.go stores a "Reconnecting... n/5" notice as the run's pending error unconditionally. An error line before it (a usage-limit message) is replaced, and turn.completed then clears the notice, so the sequence error "You've hit your usage limit.", error "Reconnecting... 1/5", turn.completed ends ok where it should end with the usage-limit error. Change it so the notice is stored only when no error is stored yet or the stored error is itself a notice: an earlier error stays the run's status and error text, a completed turn clears a notice but never an error, and with no error before them a later notice replaces the earlier one. Add a test in internal/agent/session_test.go for error, notice, turn.completed keeping the error's text and status. Do not run git on this repository.

In the api backend's Run in internal/agent/api.go, when client.stream returns a partial message together with an error, the durable path returns durableFailure(err) before the message's usage is added to the result, so that turn's partial tokens, context and estimated cost are missing from the result and the checkpoint. The local path adds the usage first. Add the usage before returning on the durable path, so a stream that fails part-way records the usage it reported on both paths, while the retry without context edits stays on the local path only and the durable failure still leaves the pending model operation in the checkpoint. Add a test in internal/agent/durable_test.go that a stream failing part-way records the usage it reported, local and durable. Do not run git on this repository.

scripts/privacy-check/main.go lists the files it scans with git ls-files -z, which prints one line per index entry, so a path in an unresolved merge conflict (stages 1, 2 and 3) is scanned two or three times and each of its findings is reported that many times. Deduplicate the file list before scanning (sort it and drop repeats), as scripts/comment-check does, and add a test in scripts/privacy-check/main_test.go that makes a real merge conflict on a scanned file in a temporary repository and checks each finding is reported once. Do not run git on this repository. (A test may run git inside its own temporary repository.)
